Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consider verb

regard as

also regard as, count as

classical

Caes. BG 1.44: sēsē illum nōn prō amīcō, sed prō hoste habitūrum
Cic. Att. 13.1.2: istuc jam prō factō habeō
Traupman 296

habeō, habēre, habuī, habitum

verb, second conjugation, with prō and the ablative

consider, regard (someone or something as …)

Prō certō habēre, consider as certain (Cic. Att. 10.6.3, Lewis & Short); in numerō habēre, count among (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dūcō, dūcere, dūxī, ductum — reckon, consider (with a genitive of value or a predicate)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.24: parvī id dūcēbat (Lewis & Short)

  • putō, putāre, putāvī, putātum — think, reckon; value (with a genitive of value)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Planc. 11: magnī putāre honōrēs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • istuc jam prō factō habeō

    I consider that as good as doneCic. Att. 13.1.2

  • sēsē illum nōn prō amīcō, sed prō hoste habitūrum

    (he said) he would regard him not as a friend but as an enemyCaes. BG 1.44

See also consider, believe.
